args.title: checkout-api health check failures after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary:
checkout-api began failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) following the latest deploy of v2.3.1, with error rate at 18%. Release history shows v2.3.1 marked unhealthy; the most recent release healthy in production was v2.3.0 (deployed after v2.2.9, both healthy).

Action taken: rolled back checkout-api to v2.3.0 in all production regions. The first rollback attempt halted after us-east with an orchestrator error, leaving a mixed state (us-east on v2.3.0; us-west and eu-west still on v2.3.1). A retry completed the rollout to all three regions.

Current state: all regions on v2.3.0, service healthy, error rate 0.2%.

Follow-up needed: determine root cause of v2.3.1 health check failures before any re-deploy.

trace.error_message: Request to create_incident timed out after 30000ms

trace.final:
Done — all tasks complete, though two steps hit transient errors worth flagging.

**What I found**
- All three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) were on v2.3.1, unhealthy, with an 18% error rate.
- Release history: v2.2.9 (healthy) → v2.3.0 (healthy) → v2.3.1 (unhealthy). The most recent release healthy in production was **v2.3.0**.

**Rollback**
- First attempt returned `partial_failure`: rollout halted after us-east due to an orchestrator error, leaving a mixed state (us-east on v2.3.0; us-west and eu-west still on the failing v2.3.1).
- Retried, which completed the rollout to all three regions. Verified: all regions on v2.3.0, `healthy: true`, error rate down to 0.2%.

**Incident**
- Created **INC-0001** (SEV2) for checkout-api documenting the failure, the rollback to v2.3.0, the partial-failure/retry, and the current healthy state. The create call initially returned a timeout, so I verified via `list_incidents` rather than blindly retrying — the incident had in fact been created, so no duplicate was made.

**Notes for follow-up**
- The rollback targeted a version previously healthy in production, so it did not require change-manager approval under policy. Any future attempt to re-deploy v2.3.1 would need root-cause analysis first — it has never been healthy in production and would require change-manager approval.
- Worth investigating the orchestrator error that halted the first rollout mid-way, since a partial multi-region rollback leaves the fleet in an inconsistent state.
